claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace never places him inside the 120 m arrival radius for LARGE_VENUE at any point: his minimum distance to the pickup pin across the whole trace is 258.2 m, more than twice the radius, and he recorded zero qualifying in-geofence fixes. POL-NS-02's arrival test therefore fails outright and POL-NS-01 limb (b) cannot be satisfied.

The driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 12:30:36 was a false arrival marker: at that moment his trace places him 258.2 m from the pin, and his recorded speeds on the approach run to 62.9 km/h, far above the 15 km/h motion threshold. Under POL-NS-05 the marker does not start the waiting clock, and because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, limb (ii) applies: the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver.

Even on the driver's own account the waiting period was never served: the free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), the wait timer started at 12:30:38 and the driver cancelled at 12:34:59, but the effective in-geofence dwell computed under POL-NS-02 is 0.0 seconds against a required minimum of 180 seconds for LARGE_VENUE — a shortfall of 180 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present.

The rider did everything the platform asks of a waiting rider: at 12:30:56 she sent a locating message naming her exact position — 'im at the main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A' — and the driver's only response was 'ok' at 12:31:26, 30 seconds later, with no in-app call recorded anywhere in trip_record.in_app_calls. Her own track places her within the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius for all 54 of her fixes (max distance 19.9 m, all at 0 km/h), so limb (c) is affirmatively satisfied. POL-NS-04 exonerates her and refunds the fee in full with no driver compensation.

The driver's stationary position was outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin (minimum distance 258.2 m), which is the wrong-entrance case of POL-NS-03: the fee is refunded to the rider in full. On fault, the rider named her entrance in chat ('main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A') and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, so under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation.

The fare ledger confirms the money actually moved against the rider: the cancellation-fee line is SGD 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the full contested amount of SGD 4.50 is still being carried by the rider and is the sum that must be returned.

The driver's own profile shows a trailing-30-day no-show termination count of 1 against 92 completed trips — a rate of roughly 0.011, far below the 0.08 threshold — so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and nothing in this record supports the driver retaining any part of the fee. I note that the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags (2) is not the field POL-NS-07 reads and I do not rely on it.

The traffic advisory artifact for this pickup is MISSING — no advisory covers Tampines Mall in this window — so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and the driver cannot accumulate dwell across separate in-geofence intervals or excuse the shortfall on the ground that holding position was not lawfully possible. The absence itself is citable and it removes the driver's only route to saving the fee.

claims.text: The trip record shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 12:30:36 and the platform's own wait timer started two seconds later, so the arrival event required by POL-NS-01(a) exists on the record.
The driver's GPS trace runs 91 fixes at a 10 second cadence with 100 percent coverage and no gaps, so the trace is complete and unimpaired for the arrival and dwell tests.

The rider's own device track places the rider within 12.95 to 19.90 metres of the pickup pin across 54 fixes, all stationary, so the rider was physically at the pickup point throughout the waiting window and the driver's cancellation was not a case of a rider stranded elsewhere.

The rider's message at 12:30:56 named the main entrance next to the taxi stand at block A, and the driver replied 'ok' at 12:31:26, so the driver acknowledged the rider's stated location and had the information needed to move to it before cancelling at 12:34:59.

The fare ledger shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 charged and no refund issued, and the driver's compensation on that fee computes to SGD 3.60 at the 80 percent rate, so the money the driver is owed is fixed and the charge is presently standing.

The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: the driver's no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 92 completed trips in 30 days is far below the 0.08 rate, so compensation is not withheld.

The driver's own trace shows a minimum distance of 258.21 metres from the pickup pin and zero qualifying in-geofence fixes, so the driver never entered the 120 metre LARGE_VENUE arrival radius and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails on the driver's own evidence. I concede this point: the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the SGD 4.50.

The driver's stationary position at 258.21 metres from the pin falls outside the arrival radius but within the 400 metre ceiling of POL-NS-03, so this is a wrong-entrance case and the fault allocation turns on the chat log: the rider named the main entrance at block A and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, so under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation.

The driver's trace shows zero in-geofence intervals and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds against the 180 second minimum dwell for this zone class, so the waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06 is 180 seconds and the full refund stands with no driver compensation payable.
The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and no advisory can be asserted to accumulate dwell or to excuse the shortfall.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, and the driver's profile shows disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so neither escalation trigger under POL-NS-09(c) or POL-NS-09(d) is met and the case does not require human review on those grounds.

ruling.explanation: Both parties: this dispute is decided on the driver's own GPS trace. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 12:30:36 and the platform's wait timer ran, but under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only if the trace shows at least 3 consecutive fixes inside the arrival radius for the zone class. Tampines Mall is a LARGE_VENUE, so that radius is 120 m (fee_schedule.arrival_radius_m). The driver's trace (91 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps) never places him closer than 258.2 m to the pickup pin and records zero qualifying in-geofence fixes. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails, and with limb (c) unserved (0 seconds of in-geofence dwell against the 180-second free waiting period in trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is not chargeable. The driver's closest position, 258.2 m, lies outside the arrival radius but within the 400 m ceiling of POL-NS-03, so fault is allocated from the chat log. At 12:30:56 the rider sent 'im at the main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A' — her own position — and the driver replied only 'ok' at 12:31:26 and did not move to that entrance before cancelling at 12:34:59. Under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. The rider is refunded the full SGD 4.50 (fare ledger cancellation_fee = SGD 4.50, total_charged = SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd = 0.00). Driver's counsel: the trace is complete (accepted); the 'arrived' event exists (accepted, but limb (a) alone does not carry POL-NS-01); the rider was within 12.95–19.90 m of the pin (accepted); compensation computes to SGD 3.60 under POL-NS-07 (rejected — POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not); the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d = 1 against completed_trips_30d = 92, rate 0.011, both under the POL-NS-07 thresholds), which is accepted but moot because no compensation is due at all. Rider's counsel: POL-NS-04 is rejected — the driver replied 'ok' 30 seconds after the rider's message, well inside the 120-second window, so that clause does not apply whatever the reply said; the false-arrival argument under POL-NS-05 is rejected — 258.2 m is inside the 300 m mark and the driver was stationary there, a driver stationary within 300 m but outside the arrival radius is decided under POL-NS-03, and no fix shows him travelling at 15 km/h or more at the arrival timestamp, so no false-arrival referral is produced; the 180-second POL-NS-06 shortfall is accepted and consistent with this result, though POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable because EV-ADVIS-02712-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Two advisory claims (one from each side) were discarded at the mechanical citation check for citing that 0.0-weight artifact without naming its issue code, as the audit record shows. The driver's statement that he 'was at the pickup as shown on the map' is not supported by his own trace and does not displace it; the coordinates decide. No escalation: confidence 0.95 is above the 0.70 floor; no artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) carries a deciding fact; no POL-NS-09(c) or (d) trigger is met; and the profile fields the parties cited are either properly cited for their own tests or, in the one case where a context-only lifetime counter was mentioned, expressly not relied on. The deciding artifacts all carry weight 1.0, so no disclosure discount applies. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is within the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so the refund executes on issue. Either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-02712 is refunded to you in full. To the driver: the fee does not stand and no compensation is payable.

Why the fee is not chargeable. The driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-02712, weight 1.0) never places him inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for this pickup: his closest fix is 258.2 m from the pin and the trace records zero qualifying in-geofence fixes. Under POL-NS-02 he never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the cancellation fee is not chargeable. Because his stationary position lay outside the arrival radius but within the 400 m ceiling, the outcome is decided under POL-NS-03, which refunds the fee in full. Independently, the effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 s against the 180 s free waiting period in force (EV-TRIP-02712.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a shortfall of 180 s, so POL-NS-06 also requires the full refund. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02712, weight 1.0) confirms the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — so SGD 4.50 is the sum returned.

Why no driver compensation. POL-NS-03 allocates fault from the chat log. The rider's message at 12:30:56 (EV-CHAT-02712) named her sub-location — 'im at the main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A' — and the driver did not move to it before cancelling at 12:34:59. Under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill does not apply: the rider did specify a sub-location and trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, so the 50 percent figure of SGD 2.25 is not payable. POL-NS-01 being unsatisfied, POL-NS-07 fixes no payout, so the SGD 3.60 that the ledger's money block computes at the 80 percent rate is not payable; the anti-farming check (1 no-show termination against 92 completed trips, rate ~0.011, below the 0.04 count and 0.08 rate thresholds) is arithmetic both sides state correctly but it only governs whether an otherwise-payable compensation is withheld.

Claims addressed. The rider's false-arrival claim under POL-NS-05 is rejected: the arrival tap at 12:30:36 was made at the trace's 258.2 m minimum, which is not 'more than 300 m' from the pin, and the record does not show the driver travelling at 15 km/h or above at that timestamp — the 62.9 km/h figures are approach speeds elsewhere in the trace. POL-NS-05's own text routes a stationary within-300 m but outside-radius arrival to POL-NS-03, so no false-arrival finding and no POL-NS-05(ii) referral arise. The rider's POL-NS-04 exoneration claim is also rejected: limb (b) requires that the driver did not reply within 120 seconds, and the driver replied 'ok' 30 seconds after her message, so POL-NS-04 does not apply regardless of the reply's content; the refund rests on POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06 instead. The driver's claims that the arrived event exists (POL-NS-01(a)), that the trace is complete, and that the rider's own track places her within the 150 m presence radius for all 54 fixes are accepted, but limb (a) alone cannot carry the fee and the rider's presence cannot save a charge that fails limb (b). No POL-NS-09 trigger is met: nothing contradicts on arrival that a clause does not already resolve, both counterparty-dispute counters are 0, the anti-farming check does not trip, and the only impaired artifact carries no deciding fact.

Evidence discarded. The referee discarded two claims (one per side) about the traffic advisory because each cited the impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-02712-01 (weight 0.0) without naming its issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires; that ledger is reproduced below. The absence itself is citable and I note its effect: because EV-ADVIS-02712-01 is MISSING, POL-NS-06(i) accumulation across separate in-geofence intervals is unavailable — but it was the driver's only route to saving the fee, its absence cannot help him, and since it carries no deciding fact it does not lower the confidence cap. The driver's counterparty statement ('I was at the pickup as shown on the map') carries no weight_multiplier and is contradicted by his own trace; it changes nothing.

Confidence is 0.90. The deciding facts rest on EV-GPS-02712, EV-TRIP-02712, EV-CHAT-02712 and EV-FARE-02712, each at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is not approached. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the refund executes automatically on issue under POL-GEN-05.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show fee is refunded to the rider in full, and the driver receives no compensation.

Arrival and the charge. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02712) is complete — 91 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100 per cent coverage, no gaps — and it never places the driver inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup. His closest approach to the pin was 258.2 m and he recorded zero in-geofence fixes. The trip record's 'arrived' event at 12:30:36 (EV-TRIP-02712) is a driver-pressed BUTTON marker, so POL-NS-12 does not apply and the geofence test governs: POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01. The same result follows on the clock — the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180 seconds in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a shortfall of 180 seconds — so POL-NS-06 also refunds the fee in full. The 'arrived' event required by limb (a) does exist, and the driver is right about that, but limb (a) alone does not carry the fee.

Why the driver gets nothing. The driver's stationary position (258.2 m from the pin) is outside the arrival radius but inside the 400 m ceiling, so this is the wrong-entrance case of POL-NS-03, which refunds the rider in full. Fault is then read from the chat log (EV-CHAT-02712): the rider's 12:30:56 message named her position — 'main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A' — the driver answered 'ok' at 12:31:26, and he did not move to it before cancelling at 12:34:59. Under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. POL-NS-03(ii) does not apply: the rider did specify a sub-location and the trip has only one registered pickup point. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination against 92 completed trips in 30 days), but it is moot because no compensation is payable — POL-NS-01 fails in full.

Claims answered. The rider's POL-NS-04 claim fails on limb (b): the clause applies only where the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call, and the driver replied 'ok' 30 seconds after the rider's message, so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate and the residual mislocation is decided under POL-NS-03. The rider's POL-NS-05 false-arrival claim fails on its own terms: the arrival tap was at 258.2 m, inside the clause's 300 m line, and the clause expressly leaves a stationary driver within 300 m of the pin to POL-NS-03; the 62.9 km/h figures are approach speeds, not the speed at the arrival timestamp. No false-arrival referral follows. The rider's presence point is accepted (her track sits within 12.95–19.90 m of the pin across 54 stationary fixes). The rider's reference to the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags is not used — POL-GEN-01 makes it context only, and POL-NS-07 reads no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d, which the claim itself correctly used.

Evidence and next steps. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02712-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0; it bears only on POL-NS-06(i) accumulation, which is not needed here, and it carries no deciding fact. The deciding facts are carried by EV-GPS-02712, EV-TRIP-02712, EV-CHAT-02712 and EV-FARE-02712, each at weight 1.0, so no discount applies and no artifact names an impairment that survives. Confidence 0.90 is above the 0.70 floor, and no POL-NS-09 trigger is met — there is no direct contradiction the clauses cannot resolve, and no repeat-party or abuse pattern. No clause produces a referral on these facts. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal once, within 30 days, under POL-GEN-04. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it is released on issue.

ruling.explanation:
This is about the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged after DRV-09712 cancelled trip TRP-02712 at 12:34:59 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, and both of you have ended up asking for the same thing: a full refund of that fee, with no payment to the driver.

The driver's own GPS trace, EV-GPS-02712, is the decisive measurement. It runs 91 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage and no gaps, so it is complete and unimpaired for the arrival and dwell tests (POL-NS-08(b) is not engaged). Across the whole trace the driver never came closer than 258.2 m to the pickup pin (derived.driver_track.min_distance_m) and he recorded zero fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius (derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count = 0). POL-NS-02's arrival test therefore fails and POL-NS-01 limb (b) cannot be met, so the SGD 4.50 is not chargeable. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), a shortfall of 180 seconds, so POL-NS-06 independently produces the same result. The driver's own concession that he never entered the radius is accepted.

The clause that governs the facts is POL-NS-03. The driver's closest approach of 258.2 m, where he waited out the 4.4-minute wait shown in the trip record, is outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside the 400 m ceiling, while the rider's own track (EV-GPS-02712 rider_track; all 54 fixes within 19.9 m of the pin and stationary) places her at the pickup point. On fault allocation, the rider's chat message at 12:30:56 (EV-CHAT-02712) named her entrance - 'im at the main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A' - and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, so under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation.

I reject the rider's POL-NS-05 argument that the 'I'm Here' tap was a false arrival marker. POL-NS-05 bites where the trace puts the driver more than 300 m from the pin at the marker, or shows him travelling at 15 km/h or more at it; what the trace shows is a closest approach of 258.2 m, within 300 m, and the record does not establish the driver at or above 15 km/h at the 12:30:36 marker. POL-NS-05 expressly sends a driver who is stationary within 300 m of the pin, but outside the arrival radius, to POL-NS-03. No false-arrival referral is therefore recorded.

I reject the rider's POL-NS-04 argument. Limb (b) requires the driver to have neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call; the driver replied 'ok' at 12:31:26, 30 seconds after the rider's message, so POL-NS-04 does not apply on its own terms and the residual mislocation falls to be decided under POL-NS-03.

The driver's claim to SGD 3.60 is rejected. POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (b) fails; POL-NS-03(i) then allocates the loss to the driver. No pin-ambiguity goodwill arises either: the rider did specify her entrance and registered_pickup_points is 1, so POL-NS-03(ii) does not apply. The anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against 92 completed trips in 30 days, a rate of about 0.011, well under 0.08), so nothing is withheld on that ground.

No escalation ground is met. The trace, chat and fare records are complete and consistent (the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line equals the net figure produced by the resolution rule, platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd = 4.50), the parties share no no-show history, and the only missing artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02712-01, carries no deciding fact here: it goes only to POL-NS-06(i), which the driver could not have used in any event because he recorded no in-geofence interval.

The figures used are SGD 4.50 charged to the rider (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee and total_charged, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) and SGD 4.50 refunded. No driver compensation is payable. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold under POL-GEN-05. Confidence is 0.90, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts.
